Definition: from G4253 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run forward, i.e. outstrip, precede:--outrun, run before.
BiblicalUsage: Protrecho means to run before, to outrun, to run forward. On the morning of the resurrection, Peter and John ran together to the sepulchre, and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre. And Zacchaeus ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see Jesus, for He was to pass that way.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that both runners teach me the same thing: the one who wants to see Jesus does not walk, he runs, and he climbs if he has to.
RelatedPeople: Simon Peter; John the Apostle; Jesus
